discovery: Fluctuation theorems and nonequilibrium work relations, the foundation of stochastic thermodynamics

nominees.name: Christopher Jarzynski
nominees.affiliation: University of Maryland, College Park, USA

nominees.name: Gavin E. Crooks
nominees.affiliation: Independent researcher (formerly Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory), USA

motivation: Evans and co-workers discovered the fluctuation theorem (1993), showing that entropy-consuming trajectories occur with exponentially suppressed but exact, quantifiable probability, which put the second law on a firm statistical footing far from equilibrium. Jarzynski's equality (1997) related irreversible work to equilibrium free-energy differences, and Crooks's theorem (1999) unified these results through time-reversal symmetry of trajectories. Together they founded stochastic thermodynamics. Their exact relations have been verified precisely in single-molecule pulling, colloidal traps, electronic circuits and trapped ions. They are now routine tools for measuring free energies in biophysics. They also made it possible to extend thermodynamics to information and feedback, turning Maxwell's demon and Landauer's principle into experimentally tested physics, and they support today's quantum thermodynamics. This is a rare case in which a simple, general principle opened an entirely new field of physics.
